transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a limit increase request on the table today. Our corporate counterparty currently has an approved derivatives exposure limit of $20 million and has requested an increase to $35 million. The derivatives desk expects this increase will support additional interest-rate and foreign-exchange hedging activity. Before I make a decision, I'd like to follow our normal process and go around the table. Let's start with credit risk -- please give us your assessment of the counterparty's credit profile and any concerns with the requested increase. Then we'll hear from legal documentation on ISDA and collateral arrangements, and finally the trading desk on the business rationale. Let's begin.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important update before we proceed. I received the counterparty's updated rating assessment this morning. Under the bank's single-name limit matrix, the counterparty's current rating band permits a maximum derivatives exposure limit of exactly $28 million. This assessment has not yet been entered in the committee pack, so you wouldn't have seen it. This means that while the counterparty has requested an increase to $35 million, the rating-based cap under our own policy is $28 million. I wanted to make sure this information is on the table before we continue the discussion.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Jonah. Before we continue, I'd like to share a relevant update from legal documentation. I confirmed yesterday that the counterparty's newly signed credit-support annex permits daily variation-margin calls with a $250,000 minimum transfer amount. The executed annex is still awaiting upload to the legal repository, but it is signed and in hand. This is relevant to our collateral posture and should factor into the committee's decision on the limit increase.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Before we wrap up, I want to share something relevant from the trading desk. I confirmed with the counterparty's treasury team this afternoon that they will post exactly $4 million of cash collateral before the increased limit is activated. This confirmation is in the desk's email folder and has not yet been added to the formal exposure request package. I think this is important for the committee to factor into the decision, particularly alongside Jonah's rating-based cap and Mei's CSA update.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Ensure the updated rating assessment is entered into the committee pack and reflected in the limit matrix records.
Ensure the executed credit-support annex is uploaded to the legal repository and linked to the counterparty's file.
Confirm receipt of the $4 million cash collateral before the increased limit is activated.
